candidates.attacker_control: An unauthenticated HTTP request header: Content-Type. The value must contain the literal substring 'multipart/form-data' (to reach the parser) while not starting with 'multipart/' (so commons-fileupload raises InvalidContentTypeException and echoes the header in its message). The value may embed a %{...} OGNL expression, which is then evaluated during error-message construction before any action/authorization logic runs.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: I verified in-tree that: (1) request wrapping precedes action mapping in both FilterDispatcher and the ng PrepareOperations/StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter; (2) the InvalidContentTypeException bundle key is absent from every struts-messages*.properties file, so the default-message branch (and thus the OGNL eval) is taken; (3) the ActionContext/ValueStack and Container are available when wrapping occurs, so translateVariables does not fail early; (4) the Content-Type check is 'contains', not 'startsWith', which is what lets a payload-bearing header reach the parser. Counterevidence/limits: the exact exception message text lives in the external commons-fileupload dependency, whose source is not present in this snapshot (the managed version is not pinned in-tree either), and I could not run anything to confirm it; the payload must satisfy both the contains() and the not-starts-with-multipart constraints in one header; configurations that replace/disable the multipart parser or bypass request wrapping are not affected.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution in the application/container JVM (the evaluated text is the attacker's Content-Type), plus an error-message injection primitive for the sibling parsers. This is exploitable on the default configuration of any Struts 2 app that accepts requests through the standard filter; no uploaded file, valid action mapping, session or credentials are required.
candidates.prerequisites: Struts 2 web application using the standard dispatcher/filter (FilterDispatcher, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter or StrutsServlet) so Dispatcher.wrapRequest() runs before action mapping; default multipart parser 'jakarta' (default in this snapshot); commons-fileupload throws InvalidContentTypeException with the raw Content-Type included in getMessage(), and no bundle entry exists for the derived message key (verified in struts-messages.properties/its locale variants: only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException are defined); ActionContext/ValueStack and its Container are already initialized at wrap time (verified in FilterDispatcher.doFilter and PrepareOperations.wrapRequest).
candidates.root_cause: The multipart error path passes attacker-influenced exception text as a localizable default message into an OGNL-evaluating lookup. JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() catches parsing exceptions and buildErrorMessage() calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), key, locale, e.getMessage(), args) (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/multipart/JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:101-124). For commons-fileupload's InvalidContentTypeException the message text contains the raw request Content-Type header; the 'struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException' key is not defined in struts-messages*.properties (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException are), so LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() falls back to that message and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/util/LocalizedTextUtil.java:668-691, eval at 683), which parses and evaluates %{...} expressions on the action ValueStack via OgnlTextParser/stack.findValue. Because request wrapping happens before action mapping, any request whose Content-Type contains 'multipart/form-data' is parsed (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/Dispatcher.java:831-847, check at 837-838; default parser 'jakarta' per core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:69 and struts-default.xml:92), so a Content-Type such as '%{<OGNL>}.multipart/form-data' is wrapped, rejected as a non-multipart content type with the raw header echoed in the exception message, and then evaluated as OGNL. The same pattern exists in sibling code: JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage/buildMessage (lines 538-557) and MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (lines 106-112).
candidates.title: Unauthenticated OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled Content-Type via multipart error message
candidates.trace: HTTP request -> FilterDispatcher/PrepareOperations creates ActionContext + ValueStack -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest(): content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper(...) -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() -> parseRequest()/ServletFileUpload.parseRequest() -> commons-fileupload InvalidContentTypeException (message includes the raw Content-Type) -> catch(Exception) -> buildErrorMessage() -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(Class, key, locale, e.getMessage(), args) -> key missing from bundles -> getDefaultMessage() -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) -> OgnlTextParser evaluates %{...} -> OgnlValueStack/OgnlUtil -> arbitrary OGNL execution in the container JVM.
candidates.unverified: The commons-fileupload behavior (InvalidContentTypeException message containing the raw Content-Type) is inferred from the well-known exploitation of this code path, not verified against dependency source in this snapshot; no runtime execution, test run or scanner was performed. Whether every deployment reaches this path (custom filters/multipart settings) is app-dependent.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression language injection / remote code execution (CWE-917)

coverage_summary: P1 relation scope: index complete for all 3401 readable source files (0 missing, 0 hash mismatches; symbols 18778, calls 38454, edges 37870, facts 468), but the index is syntactic navigation only — no data-flow, reachability or exploitability claims; its only 'injection'/'security_call' facts are name-based hints and were treated as leads, not findings. Source review covered the core request pipeline (FilterDispatcher, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter/PrepareOperations, Dispatcher, wrapRequest, multipart parsers and wrapper, SessionMap/ApplicationMap/RequestMap, static content loader, all result classes incl. redirect/XSLT/stream/httpheader), the action mapping layer (DefaultActionMapper, RestActionMapper, Restful2ActionMapper, Composite/PrefixBased mappers, ActionMapping, DefaultActionProxy/Invocation, ActionConfig/AllowedMethods/XmlConfigProvider/ActionConfigMatcher), xwork OGNL/security (OgnlUtil, OgnlValueStack, OgnlTextParser, TextParseUtil, LocalizedTextUtil, SecurityMemberAccess, accepted/excluded pattern checkers, reflection/accessors, Parameters/Alias/StaticParameters/Cookie/Scope/Chaining/MessageStore/I18n/Roles/Token/FileUpload interceptors), the StrutsConstants/default.properties/struts-default.xml/xwork-default.xml configuration, and the rest, json, codebehind, convention, oval and embeddedjsp plugins plus apps/bundles where relevant. Binary-like files and any src/test trees are absent from the snapshot, so no build, test, scanner or runtime evidence exists for any file.
limitations: No code execution, tests, builds or scanners were run; every conclusion is static source reading.
No src/test directories exist in the snapshot, so intended-behavior checks could not be derived from tests.

No git history/patch is available: I could not diff against upstream, so I cannot prove which hunks were seeded/reverted; several 'missing hardening' observations (struts-default.xml excludeParams/strict-method-invocation, RestActionMapper cleanup) could be upstream state at this revision.

The candidate depends on external dependency behavior (commons-fileupload InvalidContentTypeException message text; the dependency version is managed outside this tree) and on servlet-container/OGNL execution semantics that were not executed or inspected in binary form.
The relation index covers all files syntactically but supplies no data flow, complete call graph, runtime reachability or vulnerability verdicts.

Breadth limits: dojo/javascript assets, embedded Tomcat/Jasper code, JSF/tiles/sitemesh/spring/cdi/osgi/plexus/dwr/jasperreports/gxp/portlet bundles and sample apps were only spot-checked, so an equally or more severe issue in those areas cannot be excluded.

rejected_leads.lead: RestActionMapper sets an arbitrary method from the URL path '/action/id/method' without the allowDynamicMethodCalls gate or cleanupActionName (plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/RestActionMapper.java:212-225), and its parseNameAndNamespace/getMapping skip cleanupActionName used by the hardened DefaultActionMapper (lines 293, 361-362).
rejected_leads.reason: Real inconsistency and a plausible DMI/access-control gap, but the method string is used for reflective method lookup and string comparison, not directly for OGNL evaluation; a working exploit needs an app-specific evaluation sink (e.g., results/chains referencing the action name) and DMI/strict-method-invocation settings. Not verifiable in-tree, weaker evidence than the candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: core/src/main/resources/struts-default.xml defaultStack/basicStack/paramsPrepareParamsStack params refs have no excludeParams, and the struts-default package has no strict-method-invocation="true" (lines 176, 229-346).
rejected_leads.reason: Could not confirm the upstream state for this revision; the DefaultExcludedPatternsChecker still covers the security-relevant patterns (struts/session/request/#/%{, class and ^(action|method):), and the strict-method-invocation mechanism only takes effect when an app enables package strictness, so impact is uncertain.

rejected_leads.lead: CookieInterceptor populates action properties from cookie names/values via stack.setValue without setting ReflectionContextState.DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/CookieInterceptor.java:320-347), unlike Parameters/Alias/StaticParameters interceptors.
rejected_leads.reason: The cookie-name allowlist ([a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+) and the excluded-pattern check block parentheses, '#', '%', '{' and 'class' navigation, so no demonstrated OGNL execution path; the missing deny flag alone is a hardening gap, not a proven vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: bundles/admin exposes an OSGi Felix shell command action (execCommand -> BundlesAction/ShellAction) and a 'bundle_*!*' wildcard method mapping (bundles/admin/src/main/resources/struts.xml:31-43).
rejected_leads.reason: This is the by-design OSGi administration console bundle, not framework core, and the same code exists upstream; no weakening relative to its intended privileged role could be established.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultStaticContentLoader path handling (cleanupPath/buildPath, endsWith check) and ServletRedirectResult/XSLTResult/Include traversal-or-redirect logic.
rejected_leads.reason: Inspection found the expected guards (resource-URL endsWith check, prohibited result params, Include '..' normalization); no concrete attacker-controlled bypass was identified.

summary: Review of the assigned Apache Struts 2 snapshot (pom version 2.3.29-SNAPSHOT; 3401 readable files; no src/test trees present). I traced attacker-controlled input through the request-wrapping, multipart parsing, mapper, parameter/interceptor, OGNL/security and plugin code. The strongest candidate is an unauthenticated expression-language injection in the multipart error path: an attacker-controlled Content-Type that both passes Dispatcher.wrapRequest()'s contains("multipart/form-data") check and fails commons-fileupload's multipart validation ends up, via the exception message, as the default text of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(), which unconditionally evaluates that text (including %{...}) against the action ValueStack with OGNL. This is the highest-impact, best-evidenced issue in the snapshot. Other suspicious-but-unconfirmed items are listed as rejected leads.
